Accordion.canExpandMultiple: True to let several sections stay open at once; otherwise opening one closes the others. Defaults to false.
Accordion.classNames: Additional CSS classes for the slots
Accordion.defaultExpandedKeys: The ids expanded at the start, for an uncontrolled accordion.
Accordion.expandedKeys: The ids of the expanded sections, for a controlled accordion; pair it with `onExpandedChange`.
Accordion.hideSeparator: Hide separator lines between accordion items
Accordion.isCollapsible: Whether expanded items can be collapsed
Accordion.isDisabled: True to show every section but refuse expanding or collapsing any of them.
Accordion.items: The items, in order. The collection never sorts or filters them: the query that fetched them did.
Accordion.onExpandedChange: Called with the ids now expanded each time a section opens or closes, in the order the items are in.
Accordion.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Accordion.render: Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
Accordion.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.
Accordion.styles: Styles for different parts of the accordion root
Accordion.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Accordion.variant: The surface of the accordion: `default` on the page, `surface` as a panel of its own. Defaults to `default`.

AccountConnection.accountName: The connected account, for example its email or store id; shown only while connected.
AccountConnection.animation:
Animation configuration for surface
- `"disable-all"`: Disable all animations including children
- `undefined`: Use default animations
AccountConnection.asChild:
When `true`, merges surface styling onto the single child element (Slot pattern).
The child must be one React element. Uses `Slot.View` internally.
AccountConnection.background:
Background layer rendered behind the surface content.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Surface.Background` for non-transparent
  variants when the active library theme registers default background
  content (e.g. `glass`); otherwise no layer
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely (wrap content in
  `Surface.Background` to keep the absolute-fill and clipping)
- `null`: removes the background layer

Not injected when `asChild` is `true` — the Slot pattern requires a
single child; render `Surface.Background` inside your child instead.
AccountConnection.connectedLabel: The status while connected, for example "Connected".
AccountConnection.description: What connecting does, under the name.
AccountConnection.details: A footnote under the row, usually the terms the user accepts by connecting.
AccountConnection.disconnectedLabel: The status while not connected, for example "Not connected".
AccountConnection.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
AccountConnection.isConnected: True when an account is connected.
AccountConnection.isLoading: True while connecting or disconnecting: the button shows a spinner and refuses presses.
AccountConnection.logo: The service's logo, usually a square `Avatar`. Decorative: the name beside it is read.
AccountConnection.onConnect: Called when the connect button is pressed.
AccountConnection.onDisconnect: Called when the disconnect button is pressed.
AccountConnection.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
AccountConnection.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.
AccountConnection.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
AccountConnection.title: The service's name, for example "Stripe" or "Talabat".
AccountConnection.variant: The surface level of the card; `transparent` drops the background and shadow. Defaults to `default`.

ActionMenu.align: Where along that side it lines up with the trigger. Defaults to `center`.
ActionMenu.animation:
Animation configuration for menu root
- `"disable-all"`: Disable all animations including children
- `true` or `undefined`: Use default animations
ActionMenu.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
ActionMenu.icon: The icon of the button: an icon name or any icon element. Defaults to `ellipsis`, which the app registers.
ActionMenu.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
ActionMenu.isDisabled: True to refuse opening the menu; the button shows the disabled style.
ActionMenu.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.
ActionMenu.label: The accessible name of the button, read in place of its icon, for example "Actions for order 1001".
ActionMenu.onAction: Called with the key of every action chosen, after the action's own `onPress`.
ActionMenu.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
ActionMenu.placement: The side of the trigger it opens on, by reading direction. The runtime flips it when there is no room.
ActionMenu.presentation:
Presentation mode for the menu content
- 'popover': Default floating popover with positioning
- 'bottom-sheet': Bottom sheet modal presentation
ActionMenu.sections: The groups of actions, in order, with a divider between them.
ActionMenu.size: The size of the button. Defaults to `md`.
ActionMenu.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
ActionMenu.variant: The emphasis of the button. Defaults to `ghost`, which sits quietly in a row.

AddressField.countries: The countries offered; defaults to every country.
AddressField.defaultCountry: The country a new address starts on; defaults to `SA`.
AddressField.defaultValue: The starting value, for an uncontrolled field.
AddressField.description: Help text under the field, tied to it for assistive technology.
AddressField.errorMessage: What is wrong, shown under the field while `isInvalid` is true, and read out with the field.
AddressField.isDisabled: True to refuse input and show the disabled style; the field leaves the tab order and is left out of the submit.
AddressField.isInvalid: True to show the error state; the field alone never decides, so a form adapter sets it from its validation.
AddressField.isReadOnly: True to show the value but refuse changes; unlike disabled, the field keeps focus and is submitted.
AddressField.isRequired: True when the form cannot be submitted without a value; the label shows it and assistive technology is told.
AddressField.label: The visible label; it is the field's accessible name, so a field without one needs the runtime's own name prop.
AddressField.name: The name the value is submitted under in a form, and the key a form adapter binds.
AddressField.onChange: Called with the new value each time the user changes it.
AddressField.value: The current value, for a controlled field; pair it with `onChange`.

AiMark.isLabelVisible: True to show the label beside the mark; required on content shown to consumers.
AiMark.kind: What the mark says: the agent can run it, an agent changed it, or AI generated it.
AiMark.label: What the mark means, in the app's language (`Your assistant can do this`); read by screen readers.
AiMark.size: The mark's size; `sm` when left out.

Alert.actions: Buttons or links for the reader's next step, drawn under the description in a wrapping row.
Alert.background:
Background layer rendered behind the alert surface.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Alert.Background` when the active
  library theme registers default background content (e.g. `glass`);
  otherwise no layer
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely (wrap content in
  `Alert.Background` to keep the absolute-fill and clipping)
- `null`: removes the background layer
Alert.description: Detail under the title: what to do next, or why.
Alert.icon: An icon in place of the tone's own, or `false` for none. Left out, the tone's icon is drawn.
Alert.id: Unique identifier for the alert. Auto-generated when not provided
Alert.render:

This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

Alert.style: Additional styles applied to the root container
Alert.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Alert.title: What happened, in the app's language and a few words. Required: it is the first thing a screen reader says.
Alert.tone: The kind of message. Defaults to `default`; `danger` and `warning` are announced at once.

AlertDialog.aria-describedby: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
AlertDialog.aria-details:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.
AlertDialog.aria-label: Defines a string value that labels the current element.
AlertDialog.aria-labelledby: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
AlertDialog.cancelLabel: The label of the button that refuses, in the app's language, for example "Keep project". On web it takes focus first; on native it comes first in reading order.
AlertDialog.children: Anything more the decision needs, shown under the description: a field to type a name into, say.
AlertDialog.confirmLabel: The label of the button that agrees, in the app's language, for example "Delete project".
AlertDialog.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
AlertDialog.description: What the decision does, read out with the dialog; text, because it is what the dialog is described by.
AlertDialog.forceMount:
Whether to force mount the component in the DOM
Useful for animation purposes when component needs to be present but hidden
AlertDialog.icon: An icon in place of the tone's own, or `false` for none. Left out, the tone's icon is drawn.
AlertDialog.isConfirmDisabled: True to refuse the confirming press until the decision is ready, as when the user must still type a name.
AlertDialog.isDismissable:
True, the default, to close the overlay on a press outside it (the backdrop on a modal, a drawer and a dialog).
Set false for a step the user must finish, and give the content its own close control.
AlertDialog.isEntering:
Whether the dialog is currently performing an entry animation. Focus is not moved into the
dialog until the animation completes, since moving the screen reader cursor may cause scrolling
that interrupts the animation.
AlertDialog.isKeyboardDismissDisabled:
True to keep the Escape key from closing the overlay. It is for a flow with unsaved work or a nested overlay
open, so set it only with `isDismissable` false or a close control in reach. Native has no Escape key, so it
stays unread there unless a component's own page says it maps to the Android back button.
AlertDialog.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.
AlertDialog.onCancel: Called when the user refuses: the cancel button, Escape or the Android back button, or a press outside.
AlertDialog.onConfirm: Called when the user confirms, just before the dialog closes.
AlertDialog.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
AlertDialog.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.
AlertDialog.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
AlertDialog.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
AlertDialog.title: The question, required: it names the dialog for assistive technology, so word it as a decision.
AlertDialog.tone: The kind of message. Defaults to `default`; `danger` and `warning` are announced at once.

AngleSlider.defaultValue: The starting angle, for an uncontrolled slider; defaults to 0.
AngleSlider.hasMarks: True to draw ticks at 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees.
AngleSlider.isDisabled: True to show the angle but refuse changes.
AngleSlider.label: The slider's visible name, for example "Gradient angle".
AngleSlider.onChange: Called with each new angle, 0 to 359.
AngleSlider.size: The dial's width and height in pixels (points on native); defaults to 160.
AngleSlider.step: The degrees one arrow key or drag stop moves; defaults to 1. Shift and Page Up/Down move 15 steps.
AngleSlider.value: The angle in degrees, for a controlled slider.

AppHeader.endContent: A node at the logical end of the bar, after its main content.
AppHeader.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
AppHeader.label: The spoken name of the region, for example "Main navigation"; required when the page holds two of its kind.
AppHeader.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
AppHeader.search: The search slot, usually a `SearchField` or a button that opens the command palette; it takes the room left over.
AppHeader.startContent: A node at the logical start of the bar, before its main content.
AppHeader.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
AppHeader.title: The app's name or logo, drawn after `startContent`; a string is drawn as semibold text.
AppHeader.userMenu: The user's menu, usually a `Menu` on an avatar; it is the last part of the bar.

AppShell.children: The page: it is drawn inside the one `main` landmark of the shell.
AppShell.collapseBelow: The breakpoint under which the frame collapses; AppShell defaults to `md` and TwoColumnLayout to `lg`.
AppShell.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
AppShell.frame:
The frame: `flush` (the default) draws the page straight on the background; `inset` draws the header and page as
a rounded card on the app's background, clear of the edges, the look a split `SidePanel` beside it matches.
AppShell.header: The bar above the page, usually an `AppHeader`.
AppShell.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
AppShell.isEmbedded: True when the shell sits inside another page: it fills its box and draws no `main` landmark or skip link.
AppShell.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.
AppShell.mainId: The id of the main region, the skip link's target. Defaults to `main-content`.
AppShell.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
AppShell.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
AppShell.sidebar: The sidebar, usually a `Sidebar`; a function receives where it is drawn. Left out, the shell has no sidebar.
AppShell.skipLabel: The text of the skip link. Defaults to the `ui` catalogue's phrase in the active locale.
AppShell.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

AreaChart.annotations: Notes pinned to categories (a launch, an outage): a dashed guide through each with its label at the top.
AreaChart.className: Classes for the figure, such as a width or margin.
AreaChart.curve: How the edge joins its points; `monotone` by default.
AreaChart.height: The plot's height in pixels; 240 by default.
AreaChart.isNormalized:
With `stacked`, stacks each category to 100%: every series is drawn as its share of the category's total and the
value axis reads in percent (area and bar charts). The tooltip and data table keep the real values.
AreaChart.label: The chart's accessible name and the data table's caption, such as "Visitors, last six months".
AreaChart.palette: The colours series take by position: `accent` steps (the default) or the `categorical` set.
AreaChart.references: Target lines and threshold bands on the value axis, drawn behind the series.
AreaChart.secondaryKeys:
The keys of the series read against a second value axis at the reading end (the left in Arabic), for two measures
of different size on one chart (orders and revenue). Vertical charts only; references stay on the first axis.
AreaChart.series: The series drawn, in legend order.
AreaChart.showBrush:
Adds a brush under the plot to zoom into a span of the categories (web line, area and composed charts; native
reads every row and ignores it). Off by default.
AreaChart.showComparison: Draws each series' `compareKey` values as a dashed twin: the previous period beside this one. Off by default.
AreaChart.showGrid: Draws the horizontal grid lines; on by default.
AreaChart.showLegend: Shows the legend under the plot; on by default when there are two series or more.
AreaChart.showTooltip: Shows the values of the pointed or pressed row; on by default.
AreaChart.showValueAxis: Draws the value axis; off by default, since the tooltip and the data table carry the values.
AreaChart.stacked: Stacks the series on one another; side by side (bars) or overlapping (areas, lines) by default.
AreaChart.syncId:
Charts that share a `syncId` point at the same row together: pointing one moves the others' crosshair and tooltip
(web; native reads one chart at a time and ignores it).
AreaChart.valueFormat: How values are written: `{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }`, `{ notation: "compact" }`.
AreaChart.valueScale:
The value axis' scale: `linear` (the default) or `log` for values that span several powers of ten. On a log scale
a value of zero or below is not drawn; use it on lines and unstacked charts.
AreaChart.xFormat: Writes the category as a date in the locale (`{ month: "short" }`); categories are shown as given without it.
AreaChart.xKey: The key of each row's category: a month name, an ISO date.

AspectRatio.children: The media, which fills the box: an image, a video or a map.
AspectRatio.ratio: Width divided by height, for example `16 / 9`, `4 / 3` or `1`. Defaults to 1.

AttachmentCard.error:
Why the upload failed; given, the card shows it in the danger tone (an empty string says "Upload failed"), with a
retry button when `onRetry` is set.
AttachmentCard.name: The file name, shown as given (never translated); it also names the card's actions.
AttachmentCard.onDownload: Called by the download button; left out, there is none.
AttachmentCard.onOpen: Called when the name is pressed, to open or preview the file; left out, the name is plain text.
AttachmentCard.onRemove: Called by the remove button; left out, there is none.
AttachmentCard.onRetry: Called by the retry button of a failed upload; left out, there is none.
AttachmentCard.previewSrc: An image of the file (an image's own URL, a PDF's first page), drawn in place of the type mark.
AttachmentCard.progress: How far an upload is, 0 to 100; given, the card shows the upload's bar in place of the type and size.
AttachmentCard.size: The size in bytes, written in the locale's digits and unit.
AttachmentCard.type: The MIME type, which picks the type mark; left out, the extension picks it.

Avatar.animation: Animation configuration. Use `"disable-all"` to disable all animations including children
Avatar.background:
Background layer rendered behind the avatar content.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Avatar.Background` for the
  combinations whose background uses the default color (default
  variant, or soft variant with `color="default"`) when the active
  library theme registers default background content (e.g. `glass`);
  otherwise no layer
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely (wrap content in
  `Avatar.Background` to keep the absolute-fill and clipping)
- `null`: removes the background layer
Avatar.fallback: An element drawn in place of the initials, usually an `Icon`; sized and coloured like the initials.
Avatar.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
Avatar.label: The accessible name; without it the avatar is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
Avatar.name: The person's or organisation's name; its initials are drawn when there is no image.
Avatar.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Avatar.shape: A circle for people, a rounded square for organisations. Defaults to `circle`.
Avatar.size: The diameter and the text size of the initials. Defaults to `md`.
Avatar.src: The image URL; the fallback shows when it is missing or fails to load.
Avatar.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Avatar.tone: The colour role of the initials and fallback icon. Defaults to `default`.
Avatar.variant: The background behind the fallback: neutral or the tone's soft colour. Defaults to `default`.

AvatarGroup.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
AvatarGroup.items: The people, in the order they stack (the first on the inline-start side).
AvatarGroup.label: The group's accessible name, for example "Assigned staff".
AvatarGroup.max: How many avatars show before a "+N" count stands for the rest. Defaults to 4.
AvatarGroup.overlap:
How stacked avatars overlap visually.
- `"clip"` — crescent mask (transparent seam; no box-shadow)
- `"ring"` — solid box-shadow outline via `--background`
Has no effect when `isGrid` is true.
AvatarGroup.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).

This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

AvatarGroup.shape: A circle for people, a rounded square for organisations. Defaults to `circle`.

Either view styles or a function that receives a boolean reflecting whether
the component is currently pressed and returns view styles.

BackToTop.className: Styles the button's wrapper, for example to move it above a bottom bar.
BackToTop.focusTargetId:
The id of the element that takes focus once at the top, for example the skip link's target or the page's `h1`.

BackToTop.label: The button's accessible name. Defaults to the catalogue's "Back to top".

Card.animation: Animation configuration. Use `"disable-all"` to disable all animations including children
Card.asChild:
When `true`, merges surface styling onto the single child element (Slot pattern).
The child must be one React element. Uses `Slot.View` internally.
Card.background:
Background layer rendered behind the surface content.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Surface.Background` for non-transparent
  variants when the active library theme registers default background
  content (e.g. `glass`); otherwise no layer
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely (wrap content in
  `Surface.Background` to keep the absolute-fill and clipping)
- `null`: removes the background layer

Not injected when `asChild` is `true` — the Slot pattern requires a
single child; render `Surface.Background` inside your child instead.
Card.children: The card's parts, usually a header, content and footer; any element is allowed.
Card.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
Card.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Card.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.
Card.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Card.variant: The surface level of the card; `transparent` drops the background and shadow. Defaults to `default`.

ComboBox.onFocus: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.
ComboBox.onFocusChange: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.
ComboBox.onInputChange: Called with the text each time the user types, which is where an async ComboBox starts its search.
ComboBox.onKeyDown: Handler that is called when a key is pressed.
ComboBox.onKeyUp: Handler that is called when a key is released.
ComboBox.onLoadMore: Called when the user scrolls to the end of the list, to fetch the next page of choices.
ComboBox.onOpenChange: Handler called when the open state changes
ComboBox.onSelectionChange: Handler called when the selection changes
ComboBox.placeholder: Text shown while the field is empty; it hints at what to pick and never replaces the label.
ComboBox.presentation:
Presentation mode for the select content
- 'popover': Default floating popover with positioning
- 'bottom-sheet': Bottom sheet modal presentation
- 'dialog': Modal dialog presentation
ComboBox.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
ComboBox.render: Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
ComboBox.selectionMode: One choice at a time. This is the default.
ComboBox.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
ComboBox.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.
ComboBox.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
ComboBox.validate: A function that returns an error message if a given value is invalid. Validation errors are displayed to the user when the form is submitted if `validationBehavior="native"`. For realtime validation, use the `isInvalid` prop instead
ComboBox.validationBehavior: Whether to use native HTML form validation to prevent form submission when the value is missing or invalid, or mark the field as required or invalid via ARIA
ComboBox.value: The current value, for a controlled field; pair it with `onChange`.
ComboBox.variant: The variant of the combo box.

CommandPalette.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
CommandPalette.hotkey: The key that opens it with Cmd or Ctrl (web); `k` by default, `false` for none.
CommandPalette.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.
CommandPalette.onAction: Called with the id of the command chosen; the palette then closes.
CommandPalette.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
CommandPalette.placeholder: The search field's hint; "Search commands" by default.
CommandPalette.sections: The groups of commands to offer, in order.

CommentThread.comments: The comments to show, oldest first.
CommentThread.isResolved: True when the thread is marked resolved.
CommentThread.label: The thread's accessible name, such as "Comments on line 3".
CommentThread.onReply: Called with the reply's text and the ids of the people it mentions.
CommentThread.onResolvedChange: Called with the new resolved state; no resolve button without it.

ComposedChart.annotations: Notes pinned to categories (a launch, an outage): a dashed guide through each with its label at the top.
ComposedChart.height: The plot's height in pixels; 240 by default.
ComposedChart.isNormalized:
With `stacked`, stacks each category to 100%: every series is drawn as its share of the category's total and the
value axis reads in percent (area and bar charts). The tooltip and data table keep the real values.
ComposedChart.label: The chart's accessible name and the data table's caption, such as "Visitors, last six months".
ComposedChart.lineKeys: The keys of the series drawn as lines; by default the last series is the line and the rest are bars.
ComposedChart.palette: The colours series take by position: `accent` steps (the default) or the `categorical` set.
ComposedChart.references: Target lines and threshold bands on the value axis, drawn behind the series.
ComposedChart.secondaryKeys:
The keys of the series read against a second value axis at the reading end (the left in Arabic), for two measures
of different size on one chart (orders and revenue). Vertical charts only; references stay on the first axis.
ComposedChart.series: The series drawn, in legend order.
ComposedChart.showBrush:
Adds a brush under the plot to zoom into a span of the categories (web line, area and composed charts; native
reads every row and ignores it). Off by default.
ComposedChart.showComparison: Draws each series' `compareKey` values as a dashed twin: the previous period beside this one. Off by default.
ComposedChart.showGrid: Draws the horizontal grid lines; on by default.
ComposedChart.showLegend: Shows the legend under the plot; on by default when there are two series or more.
ComposedChart.showTooltip: Shows the values of the pointed or pressed row; on by default.
ComposedChart.showValueAxis: Draws the value axis; off by default, since the tooltip and the data table carry the values.
ComposedChart.stacked: Stacks the series on one another; side by side (bars) or overlapping (areas, lines) by default.
ComposedChart.syncId:
Charts that share a `syncId` point at the same row together: pointing one moves the others' crosshair and tooltip
(web; native reads one chart at a time and ignores it).
ComposedChart.valueFormat: How values are written: `{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }`, `{ notation: "compact" }`.
ComposedChart.valueScale:
The value axis' scale: `linear` (the default) or `log` for values that span several powers of ten. On a log scale
a value of zero or below is not drawn; use it on lines and unstacked charts.
ComposedChart.xFormat: Writes the category as a date in the locale (`{ month: "short" }`); categories are shown as given without it.
ComposedChart.xKey: The key of each row's category: a month name, an ISO date.

ConfirmationProvider.children: The app the provider wraps; any component below it can call `useConfirmation()`.

ContextMenu.children: The area that answers a right-click or a long press: a row, a card, a canvas.
ContextMenu.isDisabled: True to open no menu: on web the browser's own menu opens instead.
ContextMenu.label: The menu's accessible name, such as "Order actions".
ContextMenu.onAction: Called with the id of the chosen action, after its own `onPress`.

ContextualHelp.UNSTABLE_portalContainer:
The container element in which the overlay portal will be placed. This may have unknown
behavior depending on where it is portalled to.
ContextualHelp.align: Where along that side it lines up with the trigger. Defaults to `center`.
ContextualHelp.alignOffset: Offset along the alignment axis in pixels
ContextualHelp.aria-describedby: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
ContextualHelp.aria-details:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.
ContextualHelp.aria-label: Defines a string value that labels the current element.
ContextualHelp.aria-labelledby: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
ContextualHelp.arrowBoundaryOffset: The minimum distance the arrow's edge should be from the edge of the overlay element.
ContextualHelp.arrowRef: A ref for the popover arrow element.
ContextualHelp.asChild: Whether to render as a child element
ContextualHelp.avoidCollisions: Whether to automatically adjust position to avoid screen edges
ContextualHelp.background:
Background layer rendered behind the popover content.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Popover.ContentBackground`, whose
  content is decided by the active library theme
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely (wrap content in
  `Popover.ContentBackground` to keep the absolute-fill and clipping)
- `null`: removes the background layer
ContextualHelp.boundaryElement: Element that that serves as the positioning boundary.
ContextualHelp.children: The help: text, or text with a link. Plain text is wrapped for the runtime.
ContextualHelp.className:
The CSS [className](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/className) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the class based on component state.
ContextualHelp.containerPadding:
The placement padding that should be applied between the element and its
surrounding container.
ContextualHelp.crossOffset:
The additional offset applied along the cross axis between the element and its
anchor element.
ContextualHelp.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
ContextualHelp.disablePositioningStyle:
Whether to disable the automatic positioning styles
Useful when you want to handle positioning manually
ContextualHelp.forceMount: Whether to force mount the component in the DOM
ContextualHelp.getTargetRect:
Overrides the target element's bounding rectangle. Useful for positioning relative to
a specific point such as the mouse cursor (e.g. context menus) or text selection.
ContextualHelp.hasArrow: True to draw an arrow from the content to its trigger. Defaults to false.
ContextualHelp.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
ContextualHelp.insets: Screen edge insets to respect when positioning
ContextualHelp.isDismissable:
True, the default, to close the overlay on a press outside it (the backdrop on a modal, a drawer and a dialog).
Set false for a step the user must finish, and give the content its own close control.
ContextualHelp.isEntering: Whether the popover is currently performing an entry animation.
ContextualHelp.isExiting: Whether the popover is currently performing an exit animation.
ContextualHelp.isKeyboardDismissDisabled:
True to keep the Escape key from closing the overlay. It is for a flow with unsaved work or a nested overlay
open, so set it only with `isDismissable` false or a close control in reach. Native has no Escape key, so it
stays unread there unless a component's own page says it maps to the Android back button.
ContextualHelp.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.
ContextualHelp.label: The accessible name of the button, which says what the help is about, for example "About tax-inclusive prices".
ContextualHelp.maxHeight:
The maxHeight specified for the overlay element.
By default, it will take all space up to the current viewport height.
ContextualHelp.offset:
The additional offset applied along the main axis between the element and its
anchor element.
ContextualHelp.onBlurWithin: Handler that is called when the target element and all descendants lose focus.
ContextualHelp.onFocusWithin: Handler that is called when the target element or a descendant receives focus.
ContextualHelp.onFocusWithinChange: Handler that is called when the the focus within state changes.
ContextualHelp.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
ContextualHelp.placement: The side of the trigger it opens on, by reading direction. The runtime flips it when there is no room.
ContextualHelp.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
ContextualHelp.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.
ContextualHelp.scrollRef: A ref for the scrollable region within the overlay.
ContextualHelp.shouldFlip:
Whether the element should flip its orientation (e.g. top to bottom or left to right) when
there is insufficient room for it to render completely.
ContextualHelp.shouldSkipAnimation:
Whether the popover should appear and disappear without an entry or exit animation. This is
used by components such as PreviewTrigger to skip animations when quickly swapping between
overlays.
ContextualHelp.shouldUpdatePosition: Whether the overlay should update its position automatically.
ContextualHelp.size: The size of the button. Defaults to `sm`, so it sits beside a label.
ContextualHelp.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
ContextualHelp.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.
ContextualHelp.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
ContextualHelp.title: The popover's heading; without it the popover is named by `label`.
ContextualHelp.triggerRef:
The ref for the element which the popover positions itself with respect to.

When used within a trigger component such as DialogTrigger, MenuTrigger, Select, etc.,
this is set automatically. It is only required when used standalone.
ContextualHelp.variant: `help` draws a question mark for how-to help, `info` an "i" for background facts. Defaults to `help`.
ContextualHelp.width:
Content width sizing strategy
- 'content-fit': Auto-size to content width (default)
- 'trigger': Match trigger width exactly
- 'full': 100% width
- number: Fixed width in pixels

ConversationList.conversations: The past conversations, in any order; the list groups them by day and puts pinned ones first.
ConversationList.label: The list's accessible name. Defaults to the catalogue's "Conversations".
ConversationList.now: "Now", for a fixed point in a test or a demo; defaults to the moment the list mounted.
ConversationList.onDelete: Called with the id when Delete is chosen; the menu offers it only when set.
ConversationList.onPinChange: Called with the id and the new state when Pin or Unpin is chosen; the menu offers it only when set.
ConversationList.onRename: Called with the id when Rename is chosen; the menu offers it only when set.
ConversationList.onSelect: Called with a conversation's id when it is chosen.
ConversationList.selectedId: The id of the conversation that is open, drawn selected.

CopyButton.animation: Animation configuration for scale and highlight feedback
CopyButton.aria-controls:
Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current
element.
CopyButton.aria-current:
Indicates whether this element represents the current item within a container or set of related
elements.
CopyButton.aria-describedby: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
CopyButton.aria-details:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.
CopyButton.aria-disabled: Indicates whether the element is disabled to users of assistive technology.
CopyButton.aria-expanded:
Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded
or collapsed.
CopyButton.aria-haspopup:
Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that
can be triggered by an element.
CopyButton.aria-labelledby: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
CopyButton.aria-pressed: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.
CopyButton.asChild:
When `true`, merges press behavior and animated scale onto the single child (Slot pattern).
The child must be one React element. Uses `Animated.createAnimatedComponent(Slot.Pressable)` internally.
CopyButton.autoFocus: Whether the element should receive focus on render.
CopyButton.background:
Background layer rendered behind the button surface.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Button.Background` for the `secondary`
  and `tertiary` variants when the active library theme registers
  default background content (e.g. `glass`); otherwise no layer
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely
- `null`: removes the background layer
CopyButton.className:
The CSS [className](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/className) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the class based on component state.
CopyButton.copiedLabel: The name and announcement once copied. Defaults to "Copied".
CopyButton.excludeFromTabOrder:
Whether to exclude the element from the sequential tab order. If true,
the element will not be focusable via the keyboard by tabbing. This should
be avoided except in rare scenarios where an alternative means of accessing
the element or its functionality via the keyboard is available.
CopyButton.feedbackVariant: Feedback variant that renders Scale + Highlight compound parts
CopyButton.form:
The `<form>` element to associate the button with.
The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.
See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/button#form).
CopyButton.formAction:
The URL that processes the information submitted by the button.
Overrides the action attribute of the button's form owner.
CopyButton.formEncType: Indicates how to encode the form data that is submitted.
CopyButton.formMethod: Indicates the HTTP method used to submit the form.
CopyButton.formNoValidate: Indicates that the form is not to be validated when it is submitted.
CopyButton.formTarget: Overrides the target attribute of the button's form owner.
CopyButton.isAnimatedStyleActive:
Whether the root's built-in animated styles (react-native-reanimated) are active.
When `false`, the animated scale style is not applied and you can implement custom logic.
CopyButton.isDisabled: True to refuse presses and show the disabled style; the button leaves the tab order on web.
CopyButton.label: The accessible name before the copy, for example "Copy order number". Defaults to "Copy".
CopyButton.name: Submitted as a pair with the button's value as part of the form data.
CopyButton.onBlur: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.
CopyButton.onClick:
**Not recommended – use `onPress` instead.** `onClick` is an alias for `onPress`
provided for compatibility with other libraries. `onPress` provides
additional event details for non-mouse interactions.
CopyButton.onCopy: Called with `value` once it is on the clipboard.
CopyButton.onFocus: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.
CopyButton.onFocusChange: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.
CopyButton.onHoverChange: Handler that is called when the hover state changes.
CopyButton.onHoverEnd: Handler that is called when a hover interaction ends.
CopyButton.onHoverStart: Handler that is called when a hover interaction starts.
CopyButton.onKeyDown: Handler that is called when a key is pressed.
CopyButton.onKeyUp: Handler that is called when a key is released.
CopyButton.onPressChange: Handler that is called when the press state changes.
CopyButton.onPressEnd:
Handler that is called when a press interaction ends, either
over the target or when the pointer leaves the target.
CopyButton.onPressStart: Handler that is called when a press interaction starts.
CopyButton.onPressUp:
Handler that is called when a press is released over the target, regardless of
whether it started on the target or not.
CopyButton.preventFocusOnPress:
Whether to prevent focus from moving to the button when pressing it.

Caution, this can make the button inaccessible and should only be used when alternative
keyboard interaction is provided, such as ComboBox's MenuTrigger or a NumberField's
increment/decrement control.
CopyButton.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
CopyButton.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.
CopyButton.size: The height, padding and text size. Defaults to `md`.
CopyButton.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
CopyButton.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.
CopyButton.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
CopyButton.type: The behavior of the button when used in an HTML form.
CopyButton.value: The text copied to the clipboard.
CopyButton.variant: The emphasis and colour of the button. Defaults to `primary`.

Countdown.from: The moment a stopwatch counts from; defaults to when it first shows.
Countdown.isRunning: False to stop the clock where it is. Defaults to true.
Countdown.label: What is being timed, for example "Offer ends in"; the timer's spoken name.
Countdown.onComplete: Called once when a countdown reaches zero.

CountrySelect.countries: The countries offered, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes; defaults to every country. Listed first: `preferred`.
CountrySelect.defaultValue: The starting value, for an uncontrolled field.
CountrySelect.description: Help text under the field, tied to it for assistive technology.
CountrySelect.errorMessage: What is wrong, shown under the field while `isInvalid` is true, and read out with the field.
CountrySelect.isDisabled: True to refuse input and show the disabled style; the field leaves the tab order and is left out of the submit.
CountrySelect.isFullWidth: True to fill the parent's width. Defaults to true.
CountrySelect.isInvalid: True to show the error state; the field alone never decides, so a form adapter sets it from its validation.
CountrySelect.isReadOnly: True to show the value but refuse changes; unlike disabled, the field keeps focus and is submitted.
CountrySelect.isRequired: True when the form cannot be submitted without a value; the label shows it and assistive technology is told.
CountrySelect.label: The visible label; it is the field's accessible name, so a field without one needs the runtime's own name prop.
CountrySelect.name: The name the value is submitted under in a form, and the key a form adapter binds.
CountrySelect.onChange: Called with the new value each time the user changes it.
CountrySelect.placeholder: Text shown while nothing is chosen.
CountrySelect.preferred: Countries pinned at the top of the list, for example the market's own.
CountrySelect.value: The current value, for a controlled field; pair it with `onChange`.

CursorPagination.count: How many items are shown now, never a total: it is announced politely when it changes. Left out, no count shows.
CursorPagination.countLabel: Writes the count as a sentence, for example "Showing 20 orders". Defaults to the `ui` catalogue's phrase in the active locale.
CursorPagination.hasMore: Whether the server has a page after this one: its `hasMore`. Without it the next button is disabled.
CursorPagination.hasPrevious: Whether an earlier page exists, which the app knows from its cursor history. Defaults to false.
CursorPagination.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
CursorPagination.isLoading: True while a page loads: the button that was pressed shows a spinner and presses are refused.
CursorPagination.label: The spoken name of the pagination landmark. Defaults to the `ui` catalogue's phrase in the active locale.
CursorPagination.loadMoreLabel: The text of the load-more button. Defaults to the `ui` catalogue's phrase in the active locale.
CursorPagination.mode: `pager` shows previous and next; `load-more` shows one button that adds the next page. Defaults to `pager`.
CursorPagination.nextLabel: The text of the next button. Defaults to the `ui` catalogue's word in the active locale.
CursorPagination.onNext: Called when the user asks for the next page (the `pager` form) or for more items (the `load-more` form).
CursorPagination.onPrevious: Called when the user asks for the previous page; the `load-more` form has no previous button.
CursorPagination.previousLabel: The text of the previous button. Defaults to the `ui` catalogue's word in the active locale.
CursorPagination.size: The height and text size of the buttons. Defaults to `md`.
CursorPagination.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

DashboardGrid.className: Classes for the grid, such as a gap or margin.
DashboardGrid.defaultLayout: The starting layout when uncontrolled, and the full set of tiles a saved layout is reconciled with.
DashboardGrid.isEditing: Shows each tile's drag handle, move and size controls (web; native lists the tiles by name to reorder). Off by default.
DashboardGrid.label: The grid's accessible name, such as "Sales overview".
DashboardGrid.layout: The layout, when the caller owns it.
DashboardGrid.layoutPort: Where an uncontrolled grid loads and saves the reader's layout.
DashboardGrid.onLayoutChange: Called with the whole new layout after each move or resize.
DashboardGrid.renderTile: Draws the tile with this id, usually a `WidgetFrame`.
DashboardGrid.tileLabel: The tile's name, read by the move and size controls and their announcements.

Editor.column: The column, which picks the input.
Editor.errorId: The id of the element that says why the draft is refused; given, the input is marked invalid and described by it.
Editor.label: The input's accessible name: the column and the row.
Editor.onCommit: Commits the draft (or `draft`, when a select hands its choice straight over) and moves on.

Field.column: The column, which picks the field.
Field.draft: The draft: text, or a boolean for a boolean column.
Field.errorMessage: The error to show under the field.
Field.label: The field's label; defaults to the column's.

DataGrid.collection:
The collection engine to arrange the columns from (`useCollection`), as DataView passes it: their order, names,
widths, pins and visibility. Left out, the grid runs its own engine over `columns`, the first `frozenColumns`
pinned to the start.
DataGrid.collectionKey: The key the grid's own engine keeps the user's column layout under; left out, nothing persists.
DataGrid.columns: The columns in reading order; the first names each row.
DataGrid.density: Web: how tall the rows are when `rowHeight` is not given: `compact` 30, `normal` 36, `roomy` 48.
DataGrid.frozenColumns: Web: how many leading columns stay in view while the grid scrolls sideways. Defaults to 1.
DataGrid.hasColumnTools:
Web: true to give each header a resize handle (drag it, or focus it and use the arrows, Home and End), drag to
reorder, and the column menu. Defaults to false.
DataGrid.height: Web: the height the rows scroll inside, as a CSS length. Defaults to `24rem`.
DataGrid.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
DataGrid.isReadOnly: True to show the values without letting them be edited.
DataGrid.label: The grid's spoken name, for example "Price list".
DataGrid.onChangesChange: Called with the pending changes each time they change, for example to warn before leaving.
DataGrid.onSave: Saves the pending changes; a returned promise keeps Save busy, and the changes clear once it resolves.
DataGrid.rowHeight: Web: the height of a row in CSS pixels; rows are virtualised at this height. Defaults to 36.
DataGrid.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
DataGrid.variant: `sheet`, the default, or `matrix`: number cells with a total per row and per column.

CollectionRowPanel.children: The page beside the panel: the table or the view.
CollectionRowPanel.item: The row open in the panel, or `null` when it is shut.
CollectionRowPanel.label: The records' name ("Orders"); the panel is named "<label> details".
CollectionRowPanel.onClose: Called when the panel is closed (its close button, Escape in the drawer).
CollectionRowPanel.renderPanel: What the panel shows for the open row.
CollectionRowPanel.title: The panel's heading for the open row, usually its row header text.

ColumnMenu.onFilterColumn: Called by "Filter by this column"; left out, there is no such item.
ColumnMenu.onStartResize: Starts a keyboard resize of the column; left out, there is no "Resize column".

CellEditor.anchor: The cell drawn under the editor; the editor covers its box.
CellEditor.column: The cell's typed column: its kind picks the DataGrid editor, its rules validate the value.
CellEditor.label: The input's accessible name: the column and the row.
CellEditor.locale: The locale the limits of an error are written in.
CellEditor.onCancel: Called when the edit is dropped (Escape).
CellEditor.onCommit: Called with a valid value; the editor closes.
CellEditor.row: The row, read by the column's own rule.

DataTable.aggregates: The aggregate of each numeric column, by column id: a heading row per group and a total row at the end show it.
DataTable.bulkActions: The actions on the selection, drawn by the bulk bar while rows are selected (`selectionMode` `multiple`).
DataTable.bulkActionsLabel: The spoken name of the bulk bar. Defaults to the table's `label` and the word "actions".
DataTable.collection:
The collection engine to draw from (`useCollection`), as DataView passes it: the columns as arranged, the sort
keys, the selection, the density, the group and the totals are its, and every change goes back to it. Left out,
the table runs its own engine over `columns`, controlled by `query`, `selectedKeys`, `groupBy`, `aggregates` and
`hiddenColumns` as before.
DataTable.collectionKey: The key the table's own engine keeps the user's column layout under (left out, nothing persists).
DataTable.defaultExpandedKeys: The ids of the rows expanded at first.
DataTable.defaultSelectedKeys: The ids selected at the start, for an uncontrolled collection.
DataTable.density: How tightly the rows are drawn: `compact`, `normal` (the default) or `roomy`. Native reads it as nothing.
DataTable.editableColumns:
The typed columns edited in place, matched to the table's columns by id: their kind picks the DataGrid editor and
their rules (required, range, the app's own) validate the value. A read-only one is not edited.
DataTable.emptyState: What the collection shows when `items` is empty and nothing is loading, usually an `EmptyState`.
DataTable.error: The thrown value of a failed fetch. Given, the table shows an `ErrorState` in place of the rows.
DataTable.errorKind: What kind of failure `error` is, so the state's wording and icon fit. Defaults to `unexpected`.
DataTable.expandedKeys: The ids of the expanded rows, for a controlled expansion.
DataTable.filterBar: What is drawn above the rows, usually a `FilterBar` given the same `query`; the table does not import it.
DataTable.filteredEmptyState:
What the table shows in place of its own "no results" state when the query narrows the records and none match.
Left out, an `EmptyState` with the `no-results` reason and a button that clears the filters.
DataTable.groupBy:
The id of a column to group the rows by: the rows on screen are gathered under a heading row per value of that
column (in the order the values first appear), which carries the group's count and aggregates.
DataTable.hasColumnTools:
True to give each header the column tools: a menu (sort, add to sort, filter, pin, hide, group, summary, resize,
move), a resize handle and drag to reorder.
DataTable.hasContextMenu: False to leave the browser's own menu on a right-click; by default a row's right-click (or Shift+F10) opens its actions.
DataTable.hasHoverActions:
True to draw the row actions that have an icon as buttons revealed on hover or keyboard focus, beside the row
menu, which still lists them all.
DataTable.hasMore: True while a cursor page after the last row exists; with `onLoadMore` it loads it when the end comes into view.
DataTable.hasPrevious: Whether an earlier page exists, which the app knows from its cursor history. Defaults to false.
DataTable.headingLevel: The level of the empty and error states' titles, so the page keeps one outline. Defaults to 3.
DataTable.hiddenColumns: The ids of the columns not drawn, usually from a `ColumnChooser`; the row-header column is always drawn.
DataTable.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
DataTable.isAllMatchingSelected: True when the user chose every matching record; the bar then reads `totalCount` as the selected count.
DataTable.isColumnResizable:
Web: true to give each header a resize handle (pointer, and the keyboard through the column menu's "Resize"); the
columns then take their `width`, `minWidth` and `maxWidth`, and the table scrolls sideways past its width.
DataTable.isLoading: True while items load: the collection is busy, and shows its loading state in place of the empty one.
DataTable.isMessageShown:
Whether the error's message is shown, as for `ErrorState`: by default outside production only, because a server
message is an internal. An app whose error carries text written for the user sets it to true.
DataTable.isStickyHeader: True to keep the header in view while the rows scroll; the table then scrolls inside `maxHeight`.
DataTable.isVirtualized:
Web: true to draw only the rows in view (the Table's virtual scrolling), for thousands of rows: the header and
the start pins stay stuck, group and detail rows scroll with the rest, and the rows scroll inside `maxHeight`.
DataTable.items: The items, in order. The collection never sorts or filters them: the query that fetched them did.
DataTable.label: The spoken name of the table, for example "Orders"; a table without one is anonymous to assistive technology.
DataTable.loadingLabel: The spoken name of what loads, for example "Loading orders"; it is read only while `isLoading` is true.
DataTable.maxHeight: The height the rows scroll inside when the header is sticky, as a CSS length. Defaults to `24rem`.
DataTable.mode: `pager` shows previous and next; `load-more` shows one button that adds the next page. Defaults to `pager`.
DataTable.onAllMatchingSelectedChange: Called with true when the user chooses all matching records and with false when they go back to the rows shown.
DataTable.onCellEdit: Called with a valid edited value; the app writes the row (a promise is awaited by nobody: report failures yourself).
DataTable.onColumnMove: Web: given, headers can be dragged to reorder the columns; called with the column and its new index.
DataTable.onColumnResize: Web: called with a column's new width, in CSS pixels, when a resize ends.
DataTable.onExpandedChange: Called with the ids of the expanded rows after a row or "expand all" is pressed.
DataTable.onFilterColumn: Called by a column menu's "Filter by this column"; left out, the menu has no such item.
DataTable.onNext: Called when the user asks for the next page (the `pager` form) or for more items (the `load-more` form).
DataTable.onPrevious: Called when the user asks for the previous page; the `load-more` form has no previous button.
DataTable.onQueryChange: Called with the whole next query each time the user changes any part of it.
DataTable.onReorder:
Given, each row gets a drag handle (pointer, keyboard and screen reader, through React Aria's drag and drop) and a
drop calls this with the rows shown in their new order (group and total rows left out). Nothing moves until the
app passes the rows back; reordering a sorted view is the app's call.
DataTable.onRetry: Called by the error state's retry button; left out, the error state has no button.
DataTable.onRowOpen: Called when a row is opened: a press on the row (Enter from the keyboard).
DataTable.onSelectionChange: Called with the ids now selected each time the selection changes, in the order the items are in.
DataTable.paginationLabel: The spoken name of the pagination landmark. Defaults to the table's `label` and the word "pagination".
DataTable.query: The query in force: the search text, the applied filters and the sort.
DataTable.renderCell:
The content of one cell. Left out, a cell shows the text of the row's property named by the column's `id`; give it
to draw a badge, a date or a link, and give the app's own text for each value, as the table adds none.
DataTable.renderRowDetail: Given, each row gets a disclosure button and an expanded row shows this under it across every column.
DataTable.renderRowPanel: Given, an opened row shows this in a resizable side panel beside the table (a drawer on a small screen).
DataTable.retryLabel: The text of the retry button. Defaults to the `ui` catalogue's word in the active locale.
DataTable.rowActions:
The actions of one row, listed in the row's menu in a last column. The handler of each closes over the row.
Left out, there is no actions column.
DataTable.scrollEnabled:
Whether the rows scroll on their own (the default). Pass `false` when the table sits inside a page's own
`ScrollView`, so the rows lay out in the page and React Native does not warn about nested lists.
DataTable.selectedKeys: The ids of the selected items, for a controlled collection; pair it with `onSelectionChange`.
DataTable.selectionMode: What a press or Space does: nothing, select one item, or toggle several. Defaults to `none`.
DataTable.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
DataTable.totalCount: How many records match the query across all pages, when the server says. Left out, "select all" is not offered.
DataTable.variant: The look of the table. Defaults to `primary`.

- `undefined`: Use default animations

  whose background uses the default color (secondary variant, or

  library theme registers default background content (e.g. `glass`);

Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.

Requirements:

Dropdown.target:

ExportDialog.columns: The columns the user may leave out, all ticked at first. Left out, there is no column picker.
ExportDialog.counts:
The row count of each scope on offer; a scope without a count is not offered, and one with 0 rows is disabled.
The narrowest scope with rows is chosen first, so a selection is exported when there is one.
ExportDialog.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
ExportDialog.deliveries: The deliveries on offer; with one, there is no picker. Defaults to `["download"]`.
ExportDialog.description: One sentence under the title: what is being exported.
ExportDialog.email: The address an emailed export goes to, shown beside the email choice.
ExportDialog.formats: The file formats (CSV, Excel, PDF); the first is chosen unless `defaultValue` says otherwise.
ExportDialog.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.
ExportDialog.onExport:
Runs the export. While its promise is pending the export button shows a spinner and a progress bar runs above
the footer; when it resolves the button turns into a done tick and the dialog closes; when it rejects the dialog
stays open with an error. Call `progress` with the share done, from 0 to 1, to fill the bar; never called, the bar
stays indeterminate.
ExportDialog.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
ExportDialog.title: The dialog's title; defaults to the catalogue's "Export".
ExportDialog.trigger: The element that opens the dialog; left out, the app opens it through `isOpen`.

Fab.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.

Fab.isExtended: True to show the label beside the icon (an extended FAB).
Fab.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.

Fab.onAction: Called with the id of every speed-dial action chosen, after the action's own `onPress`.
Fab.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
Fab.onPress: Called when the Fab is pressed; without `actions` it is the Fab's action.
Fab.placement: Where it sits. Defaults to `bottom-end`, the reading end, so bottom left in Arabic.

FeedbackIcon.icon: The caller's icon: a name or an element. Left out, the tone's icon is drawn.

ImportFlow.dryRun: The dry run's result; the flow shows the review step while it is set.
ImportFlow.fields: The fields a column can map to.

InputGroup.aria-activedescendant:
Identifies the currently active element when DOM focus is on a composite widget, textbox,
group, or application.
InputGroup.aria-autocomplete:
Indicates whether inputting text could trigger display of one or more predictions of the user's
intended value for an input and specifies how predictions would be presented if they are made.
InputGroup.aria-controls:
Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current
element.
InputGroup.aria-describedby: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
InputGroup.aria-details:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.
InputGroup.aria-errormessage: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.
InputGroup.aria-haspopup:
Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that
can be triggered by an element.
InputGroup.aria-label: Defines a string value that labels the current element.
InputGroup.aria-labelledby: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
InputGroup.autoComplete:
Describes the type of autocomplete functionality the input should provide if any. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#htmlattrdefautocomplete).
InputGroup.autoCorrect:
An attribute that takes as its value a space-separated string that describes what, if any, type
of autocomplete functionality the input should provide. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#autocomplete).
InputGroup.autoFocus: Whether the element should receive focus on render.
InputGroup.background:
Background layer rendered behind the text input.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Input.Background` when the active
  library theme registers default background content (e.g. `glass`);
  the fallback color follows the variant (primary → field token,
  secondary → default token); otherwise no layer and no wrapper
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely and wraps the text
  input (wrap content in `Input.Background` to keep absolute-fill and
  clipping)
- `null`: removes the background layer (bare text input root)
InputGroup.className:
The CSS [className](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/className) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the class based on component state.
InputGroup.containerClassName:
Additional CSS classes for the outer container that wraps the
background layer and the text input (e.g. `flex-1` in row layouts).
When no background layer is present the text input is the root element,
so these classes are merged onto it instead — root-level layout stays
consistent across themes either way.
InputGroup.defaultValue: The starting value, for an uncontrolled field.
InputGroup.description: Help text under the field, tied to it for assistive technology.
InputGroup.enterKeyHint:
An enumerated attribute that defines what action label or icon to preset for the enter key on
virtual keyboards. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/enterkeyhint).
InputGroup.errorMessage: What is wrong, shown under the field while `isInvalid` is true, and read out with the field.
InputGroup.excludeFromTabOrder:
Whether to exclude the element from the sequential tab order. If true,
the element will not be focusable via the keyboard by tabbing. This should
be avoided except in rare scenarios where an alternative means of accessing
the element or its functionality via the keyboard is available.
InputGroup.form:
The `<form>` element to associate the input with.
The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.
See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input#form).
InputGroup.inputMode:
Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its
contents. See
[MDN](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#input-modalities:-the-inputmode-attribute).
InputGroup.isDisabled: True to refuse input and show the disabled style; the field leaves the tab order and is left out of the submit.
InputGroup.isFullWidth: True to fill the parent's width, false to size to the content. Defaults to true.
InputGroup.isInvalid: True to show the error state; the field alone never decides, so a form adapter sets it from its validation.
InputGroup.isReadOnly: True to show the value but refuse changes; unlike disabled, the field keeps focus and is submitted.
InputGroup.isRequired: True when the form cannot be submitted without a value; the label shows it and assistive technology is told.
InputGroup.label: The visible label; it is the field's accessible name, so a field without one needs the runtime's own name prop.
InputGroup.maxLength:
The maximum number of characters supported by the input. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#htmlattrdefmaxlength).
InputGroup.minLength:
The minimum number of characters required by the input. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#htmlattrdefminlength).
InputGroup.name: The name the value is submitted under in a form, and the key a form adapter binds.
InputGroup.onBeforeInput:
Handler that is called when the input value is about to be modified. See

InputGroup.onBlur: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.
InputGroup.onChange: Called with the new value each time the user changes it.
InputGroup.onCompositionEnd:
Handler that is called when a text composition system completes or cancels the current text
composition session. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/compositionend_event).
InputGroup.onCompositionStart:
Handler that is called when a text composition system starts a new text composition session.
See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/compositionstart_event).
InputGroup.onCompositionUpdate:
Handler that is called when a new character is received in the current text composition
session. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/compositionupdate_event).
InputGroup.onCopy:
Handler that is called when the user copies text. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/oncopy).
InputGroup.onCut:
Handler that is called when the user cuts text. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/oncut).
InputGroup.onFocus: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.
InputGroup.onFocusChange: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.
InputGroup.onInput:
Handler that is called when the input value is modified. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/input_event).
InputGroup.onKeyDown: Handler that is called when a key is pressed.
InputGroup.onKeyUp: Handler that is called when a key is released.
InputGroup.onPaste:
Handler that is called when the user pastes text. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/onpaste).
InputGroup.onSelect:
Handler that is called when text in the input is selected. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/select_event).
InputGroup.pattern:
Regex pattern that the value of the input must match to be valid. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#htmlattrdefpattern).
InputGroup.placeholder: Hint text drawn inside the empty input. It never replaces the label: it is gone once the user types.
InputGroup.placeholderColorClassName: Custom className for the placeholder text color
InputGroup.prefix: Content before the value, on the inline-start side: short text, or an element such as an icon.

  as appropriate.

InputGroup.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
InputGroup.spellCheck:
An enumerated attribute that defines whether the element may be checked for spelling errors.

InputGroup.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the

InputGroup.suffix: Content after the value, on the inline-end side: short text, or an element such as a button.

InputGroup.variant: The look of the field: `primary` on the page, `secondary` on a tinted surface. Defaults to `primary`.

ItemCard.icon: A leading icon from the house set.

KioskSurface.reach: The reach layout; `standing` when left out.

Kpi.badge: A short tag beside the figure; nothing is drawn when it is empty.
Kpi.better: The direction that is better for the trend's colour; `up` by default.
Kpi.comparison: What the trend compares with: "vs last month".
Kpi.icon: An icon at the tile's start, beside the label.
Kpi.label: What the figure counts, shown above it.
Kpi.onPress: The drill-down: the whole tile becomes a button that opens the detail.
Kpi.pressLabel: The drill-down button's description ("Open Revenue" by default); its name is what the tile shows.
Kpi.previousValue:
The previous period's figure: a muted "Previous period" line under the figure, formatted like it, and, when

Kpi.sparkline: The recent values, oldest first, drawn as an area sparkline under the figure.
Kpi.target: The goal for a numeric `value`: a bar shows how far along it is.
Kpi.trend: The change against the previous period as a fraction (0.12 is up 12%), drawn as a `TrendChip`.
Kpi.value: The figure: a number, formatted in the locale, or text already formatted.

TrendChip.comparison: What it compares with, read after the change: "vs last month".
TrendChip.format: How the change is written; a signed percent with up to one decimal by default.
TrendChip.value: The change, as a fraction by default: 0.12 is up 12%, -0.05 down 5%, 0 flat.

KpiGroup.children: The KPIs, usually `Stat`s (a group draws one shared surface, so its members need none of their own).
KpiGroup.label: The band's accessible name, such as "This month at a glance".

Label.children: The label's text, required: a label with none names nothing. It names the field for assistive technology.
Label.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
Label.isDisabled: True to draw the label in the disabled style.
Label.isInvalid: True to draw the label in the error colour.
Label.isRequired: True to mark the field as required: the label shows an asterisk.
Label.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Label.render:

  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.
Label.style: Style properties for the label container
Label.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).

Grid.gap: The space between cells. Defaults to `md` (16px).
Grid.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
Grid.minItemWidth: The narrowest a cell may be, in pixels: the grid fits as many columns as this allows, at least one.
Grid.ref:

Stack.gap: The space between blocks. Defaults to `md` (16px).
