LeaveConfirmation.description: What leaving costs, read out with the dialog, for example "Your edits to this page will be lost.".
LeaveConfirmation.discardLabel: The label of the button that leaves and drops the changes, in the app's language.
LeaveConfirmation.stayLabel: The label of the button that stays on the page, in the app's language. It takes focus first.
LeaveConfirmation.title: The question, required, for example "Discard unsaved changes?".
LeaveConfirmation.when: True while there is unsaved work; false means leaving costs nothing and `confirmLeave` never asks.

Lightbox.defaultIndex: The position shown first, for an uncontrolled lightbox. Defaults to 0.
Lightbox.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
Lightbox.index: The position of the picture in view, for a controlled lightbox; pair it with `onIndexChange`.
Lightbox.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.
Lightbox.label: The viewer's accessible name, for example "Product photos"; defaults to the catalogue's "Image viewer".
Lightbox.onIndexChange: Called with the new position each time another picture comes into view.
Lightbox.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.

LineChart.annotations: Notes pinned to categories (a launch, an outage): a dashed guide through each with its label at the top.
LineChart.className: Classes for the figure, such as a width or margin.
LineChart.curve: How the line joins its points; `monotone` by default.
LineChart.height: The plot's height in pixels; 240 by default.
LineChart.isNormalized:
With `stacked`, stacks each category to 100%: every series is drawn as its share of the category's total and the
value axis reads in percent (area and bar charts). The tooltip and data table keep the real values.
LineChart.label: The chart's accessible name and the data table's caption, such as "Visitors, last six months".
LineChart.palette: The colours series take by position: `accent` steps (the default) or the `categorical` set.
LineChart.references: Target lines and threshold bands on the value axis, drawn behind the series.
LineChart.secondaryKeys:
The keys of the series read against a second value axis at the reading end (the left in Arabic), for two measures
of different size on one chart (orders and revenue). Vertical charts only; references stay on the first axis.
LineChart.series: The series drawn, in legend order.
LineChart.showBrush:
Adds a brush under the plot to zoom into a span of the categories (web line, area and composed charts; native
reads every row and ignores it). Off by default.
LineChart.showComparison: Draws each series' `compareKey` values as a dashed twin: the previous period beside this one. Off by default.
LineChart.showDots: Marks each point with a dot; off by default.
LineChart.showGrid: Draws the horizontal grid lines; on by default.
LineChart.showLegend: Shows the legend under the plot; on by default when there are two series or more.
LineChart.showTooltip: Shows the values of the pointed or pressed row; on by default.
LineChart.showValueAxis: Draws the value axis; off by default, since the tooltip and the data table carry the values.
LineChart.stacked: Stacks the series on one another; side by side (bars) or overlapping (areas, lines) by default.
LineChart.syncId:
Charts that share a `syncId` point at the same row together: pointing one moves the others' crosshair and tooltip
(web; native reads one chart at a time and ignores it).
LineChart.valueFormat: How values are written: `{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }`, `{ notation: "compact" }`.
LineChart.valueScale:
The value axis' scale: `linear` (the default) or `log` for values that span several powers of ten. On a log scale
a value of zero or below is not drawn; use it on lines and unstacked charts.
LineChart.xFormat: Writes the category as a date in the locale (`{ month: "short" }`); categories are shown as given without it.
LineChart.xKey: The key of each row's category: a month name, an ISO date.

object.

Link.className: Custom classes merged with the default styles
Link.download: Prompts file download instead of navigation
Link.externalLabel: What assistive technology hears for an external link. Defaults to the `ui` catalogue's phrase in the active locale.
Link.feedbackVariant: Feedback variant that renders Scale + Highlight compound parts
Link.href: Where the link goes: an app path (`/orders/ord_1`) for the router, or an absolute URL (`https:`, `mailto:`).
Link.hrefLang:

Link.isAnimatedStyleActive:

Link.onFocus: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.
Link.onFocusChange: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.
Link.onHoverChange: Handler that is called when the hover state changes.
Link.onHoverEnd: Handler that is called when a hover interaction ends.
Link.onHoverStart: Handler that is called when a hover interaction starts.
Link.onKeyDown: Handler that is called when a key is pressed.
Link.onKeyUp: Handler that is called when a key is released.
Link.onPress: Called when the link is activated, before the link follows `href`.
Link.onPressChange: Handler that is called when the press state changes.
Link.onPressEnd:
Handler that is called when a press interaction ends, either
over the target or when the pointer leaves the target.
Link.onPressStart: Handler that is called when a press interaction starts.
Link.onPressUp:
Handler that is called when a press is released over the target, regardless of
whether it started on the target or not.
Link.ping:
A space-separated list of URLs to ping when the link is followed. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#ping).
Link.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Link.referrerPolicy:
How much of the referrer to send when following the link. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#referrerpolicy).
Link.rel: Relationship between the current and linked documents
Link.render: Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
Link.routerOptions: Options for the configured client side router.
Link.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
Link.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.
Link.target: Controls where to open the linked document
Link.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Link.tone: The semantic colour of the link text. Defaults to `default`, the theme's link colour.
Link.underline: When the underline shows: `always` (default; required inside running text) or `hover` (standalone links).

Item.className: Additional CSS classes for the item
Item.description: The muted line under the title.
Item.endContent: What the row shows at its end, before the chevron: a `Chip`, a value, a switch.
Item.hasChevron: Draws a chevron at the end that points the reading way, to say that the row opens something.
Item.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
Item.isDisabled: Refuses the press and the selection of a row that has either, and dims it; a plain row has nothing to refuse.
Item.label: The accessible name when the title is not a string; also what type-ahead matches. Defaults to the title text.
Item.onPress: Makes the row a button and is called when it is pressed; without it the row is plain content.
Item.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Item.startIcon: The leading visual: an icon by name, or an element drawn as given, usually an `Avatar`.
Item.style:
Either view styles or a function that receives a boolean reflecting whether
the component is currently pressed and returns view styles.
Item.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Item.title: The row's main text, or any node when the row needs more than text.

List.defaultSelectedKeys: The ids selected at the start, for an uncontrolled collection.
List.emptyState: What the collection shows when `items` is empty and nothing is loading, usually an `EmptyState`.
List.hasMore: True while a cursor page has a next one; `onLoadMore` is called only then.
List.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
List.isAnimated:
The rows fade in and rise into place as one block when the list mounts, inside the list's surface (`Reveal`, ADR 0329). Defaults
to on; off, or under reduced motion, they show at once.
List.isLoading: True while items load: the collection is busy, and shows its loading state in place of the empty one.
List.items: The items, in order. The collection never sorts or filters them: the query that fetched them did.
List.label: The spoken name of the list, for example "Recent orders".
List.loadingLabel: The spoken name of what loads, for example "Loading orders"; it is read only while `isLoading` is true.
List.maxHeight: Web: the height a virtualised list scrolls within (any CSS length). Defaults to `32rem`.
List.onLoadMore: Called when the end of the list is reached and `hasMore` is true, never while `isLoading`.
List.onSelectionChange: Called with the ids now selected each time the selection changes, in the order the items are in.
List.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
List.scrollEnabled:
`false` for a list inside a page that scrolls the same way: the page scrolls it, and React Native nests no
virtualized list in a plain `ScrollView`. Defaults to `true`, the list scrolling on its own.
List.selectedKeys: The ids of the selected items, for a controlled collection; pair it with `onSelectionChange`.
List.selectionMode: What a press or Space does: nothing, select one item, or toggle several. Defaults to `none`.
List.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
List.variant: The surface level the rows sit on. Defaults to `default`.

Listbox.ariaLabel: The list's spoken name when it has no visible label.
Listbox.defaultValue: The starting value, for an uncontrolled field.
Listbox.description: Help text under the field, tied to it for assistive technology.
Listbox.errorMessage: What is wrong, shown under the field while `isInvalid` is true, and read out with the field.
Listbox.isDisabled: True to refuse input and show the disabled style; the field leaves the tab order and is left out of the submit.
Listbox.isInvalid: True to show the error state; the field alone never decides, so a form adapter sets it from its validation.
Listbox.isReadOnly: True to show the value but refuse changes; unlike disabled, the field keeps focus and is submitted.
Listbox.isRequired: True when the form cannot be submitted without a value; the label shows it and assistive technology is told.
Listbox.items: The options, when they are not in sections.
Listbox.label: The visible label; it is the field's accessible name, so a field without one needs the runtime's own name prop.
Listbox.name: The name the value is submitted under in a form, and the key a form adapter binds.
Listbox.onChange: Called with the new value each time the user changes it.
Listbox.sections: The options in titled groups; used instead of `items`.
Listbox.value: The current value, for a controlled field; pair it with `onChange`.

LoadingOverlay.isLoading: True while the content is loading or saving: it is covered, blocked and hidden from screen readers.
LoadingOverlay.message: What is happening, for example "Saving the price list…"; defaults to the catalogue's "Loading…".

LocaleSwitcher.label: The visible label; defaults to the `ui` catalogue's "Language".
LocaleSwitcher.locales: The locales offered, as BCP 47 tags.

Marquee.children: The items, in reading order, for example brand logos or short announcements.
Marquee.label: What the strip is, for screen readers, for example "Brands we carry".
Marquee.speed: Speed in pixels per second. Defaults to 40.

MaskedField.accessibilityLabel: The field's name for assistive technology when it has no string `label`.
MaskedField.aria-label: The field's name for assistive technology when it has no visible `label`.
MaskedField.defaultValue: The starting value, for an uncontrolled field.
MaskedField.description: Help text under the field, tied to it for assistive technology.
MaskedField.errorMessage: What is wrong, shown under the field while `isInvalid` is true, and read out with the field.
MaskedField.isDisabled: True to refuse input and show the disabled style; the field leaves the tab order and is left out of the submit.
MaskedField.isFullWidth: True to fill the parent's width, false to size to the content. Defaults to true.
MaskedField.isInvalid: True to show the error state; the field alone never decides, so a form adapter sets it from its validation.
MaskedField.isReadOnly: True to show the value but refuse changes; unlike disabled, the field keeps focus and is submitted.
MaskedField.isRequired: True when the form cannot be submitted without a value; the label shows it and assistive technology is told.
MaskedField.label: The visible label; it is the field's accessible name, so a field without one needs the runtime's own name prop.
MaskedField.mask:
The pattern: `9` takes a digit, `a` a letter, `A` a letter written upper case, `*` a letter or digit, and every
other character is written as is, for example `999 999 9999` or `AA99 9999 9999 9999 9999 9999`. Digits show in
the customer's digits and are read in Latin or Arabic-Indic.
MaskedField.name: The name the value is submitted under in a form, and the key a form adapter binds.
MaskedField.onChange: Called with the new value each time the user changes it.
MaskedField.placeholder: Hint text drawn inside the empty input. It never replaces the label: it is gone once the user types.
MaskedField.value: The current value, for a controlled field; pair it with `onChange`.
MaskedField.variant: The look of the field: `primary` on the page, `secondary` on a tinted surface. Defaults to `primary`.

MediaPlayer.label: The player's accessible name, for example the video's title.
MediaPlayer.onEnded: Called once the file plays to its end.
MediaPlayer.playbackRates: The speeds the speed menu offers; defaults to 0.5, 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 2.
MediaPlayer.poster: A still shown before a video plays.
MediaPlayer.tracks: Captions files; with any, a captions button appears and shows the one in the reader's language, else the first.

MediaRange.buffered: How far the file is loaded, drawn behind the fill; leave it out for none.
MediaRange.label: The accessible name.
MediaRange.max: The end of the range (the length in seconds, or 1 for the volume).
MediaRange.step: What one arrow key moves. Page Up and Page Down move ten times as far.
MediaRange.valueText: What a screen reader says for the value, for example "0:12 of 1:05".

MentionInput.accessibilityLabel: The box's name for assistive technology when it has no string `label`.
MentionInput.aria-label: The box's name for assistive technology when it has no visible `label`.
MentionInput.defaultValue: The starting value, for an uncontrolled field.
MentionInput.description: Help text under the field, tied to it for assistive technology.
MentionInput.errorMessage: What is wrong, shown under the field while `isInvalid` is true, and read out with the field.
MentionInput.isDisabled: True to refuse input and show the disabled style; the field leaves the tab order and is left out of the submit.
MentionInput.isInvalid: True to show the error state; the field alone never decides, so a form adapter sets it from its validation.
MentionInput.isReadOnly: True to show the value but refuse changes; unlike disabled, the field keeps focus and is submitted.
MentionInput.isRequired: True when the form cannot be submitted without a value; the label shows it and assistive technology is told.
MentionInput.label: The visible label; it is the field's accessible name, so a field without one needs the runtime's own name prop.
MentionInput.maxSuggestions: How many people the list shows at most. Defaults to 6.
MentionInput.name: The name the value is submitted under in a form, and the key a form adapter binds.
MentionInput.onChange: Called with the new value each time the user changes it.
MentionInput.onMentionsChange: Called with the ids of the people the text mentions, in the order they first appear, each time the text changes.
MentionInput.people: The people who can be mentioned; the list shows those whose name starts with what follows the `@`.
MentionInput.placeholder: Hint text inside the empty box.
MentionInput.rows: The number of lines the box shows. Defaults to 3.
MentionInput.value: The current value, for a controlled field; pair it with `onChange`.

Body.aria-describedby: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
Body.aria-details:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.
Body.aria-label: Defines a string value that labels the current element.
Body.aria-labelledby: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
Body.autoFocus: Where the focus should be set.
Body.className:
The CSS [className](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/className) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the class based on component state.
Body.defaultSelectedKeys: The initial selected keys in the collection (uncontrolled).
Body.dependencies: Values that should invalidate the item cache when using dynamic collections.
Body.disabledKeys:
The item keys that are disabled. These items cannot be selected, focused, or otherwise
interacted with.
Body.disallowEmptySelection: Whether the collection allows empty selection.
Body.escapeKeyBehavior:
Whether pressing the escape key should clear selection in the menu or not.

Most experiences should not modify this option as it eliminates a keyboard user's ability to
easily clear selection. Only use if the escape key is being handled externally or should not
trigger selection clearing contextually.
Body.onAction: Called with the key of every action chosen.
Body.onClose: Handler that is called when the menu should close after selecting an item.
Body.onSelectedChange: Called with the new chosen keys.
Body.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Body.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.
Body.renderEmptyState: Provides content to display when there are no items in the menu.
Body.sections: The groups of actions, in order, with a divider between them.
Body.selected: The chosen keys across all sections.
Body.shouldCloseOnSelect: Whether the menu should close when the menu item is selected.
Body.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
Body.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.

Menu.align: Where along that side it lines up with the trigger. Defaults to `center`.
Menu.children: The element that opens the menu, usually a `Button` or `IconButton`; it must be pressable and named.
Menu.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
Menu.defaultValue: The keys chosen at the start, for an uncontrolled menu.
Menu.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
Menu.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.
Menu.onAction: Called with the key of every action chosen, after the action's own `onPress`.
Menu.onChange: Called with the new list of chosen keys each time the selection changes.
Menu.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
Menu.placement: The side of the trigger it opens on, by reading direction. The runtime flips it when there is no room.
Menu.presentation: Presentation mode for the menu content
Menu.sections: The groups of actions, in order, with a divider between them.
Menu.selectionMode:
What choosing an action does: just run it (`none`, the default), or also keep it chosen, one per section
(`single`) or any number (`multiple`). A chosen action shows a mark and is reported in `onChange`.
Menu.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Menu.trigger: The type of interaction that triggers the menu
Menu.value: The keys of the chosen actions, for a controlled menu; pair it with `onChange`.

Menubar.aria-label: The bar's accessible name. Defaults to the catalogue's "Application menu".
Menubar.defaultValue: The keys checked at the start, for an uncontrolled menubar.
Menubar.menus: The menus, in order on the bar.
Menubar.onAction: Called with the key of every action chosen, after the action's own `onPress`.
Menubar.onChange: Called with the new list of checked keys each time a checkable action changes.
Menubar.value: The keys of the checked actions across all menus, for a controlled menubar; pair it with `onChange`.

MessageActions.copyValue: The message's text; set it to offer Copy.
MessageActions.feedback: The rating given, or null for none; set it to control the thumbs (uncontrolled when left out).
MessageActions.label: The row's accessible name. Defaults to the catalogue's "Message actions".
MessageActions.onCopy: Called with the text once it is on the clipboard.
MessageActions.onEdit: Called when Edit is pressed; set it to offer Edit.
MessageActions.onFeedbackChange: Called with the new rating, or null when a pressed thumb is pressed again; set it to offer the thumbs.
MessageActions.onRetry: Called when Retry is pressed; set it to offer Retry.

MessageScroller.children: The messages, oldest first, one child each: the jump button counts the children added since the person left.
MessageScroller.className: Styles the scrolling region; give it a height (or a flex parent) so it can scroll.
MessageScroller.label: The region's accessible name. Defaults to the catalogue's "Conversation".

Meter.formatOptions: How the value is written; defaults to a percent of the scale.
Meter.high: Where the high part of the scale starts.
Meter.label: The visible name, which is also the spoken one.
Meter.low: Where the low part of the scale ends.
Meter.optimum: The best value: its part is green, the next part amber, the far part red. Defaults to the middle.
Meter.value: The measure the bar fills to.
Meter.valueLabel: Words to show and say instead of the number, for example "8.2 of 10 GB".

Close.animation: Animation configuration for scale and highlight feedback
Close.aria-controls:
Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current
element.
Close.aria-current:
Indicates whether this element represents the current item within a container or set of related
elements.
Close.aria-describedby: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
Close.aria-details:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.
Close.aria-disabled: Indicates whether the element is disabled to users of assistive technology.
Close.aria-expanded:
Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded
or collapsed.
Close.aria-haspopup:
Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that
can be triggered by an element.
Close.aria-labelledby: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
Close.aria-pressed: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.
Close.asChild:
When `true`, merges press behavior and animated scale onto the single child (Slot pattern).
The child must be one React element. Uses `Animated.createAnimatedComponent(Slot.Pressable)` internally.
Close.autoFocus: Whether the element should receive focus on render.
Close.background:
Background layer rendered behind the button surface.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Button.Background` for the `secondary`
  and `tertiary` variants when the active library theme registers
  default background content (e.g. `glass`); otherwise no layer
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely
- `null`: removes the background layer
Close.className:
The CSS [className](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/className) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the class based on component state.
Close.closeButton:
How the control is drawn: `"esc"` (default) one button showing the Escape key cap, the close mark on a touch
screen; `"icon"` the close mark; `"both"` the key cap and the close mark in one button; `"none"` nothing.
Close.excludeFromTabOrder:
Whether to exclude the element from the sequential tab order. If true,
the element will not be focusable via the keyboard by tabbing. This should
be avoided except in rare scenarios where an alternative means of accessing
the element or its functionality via the keyboard is available.
Close.feedbackVariant: Feedback variant that renders Scale + Highlight compound parts
Close.form:
The `<form>` element to associate the button with.
The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.
See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/button#form).
Close.formAction:
The URL that processes the information submitted by the button.
Overrides the action attribute of the button's form owner.
Close.formEncType: Indicates how to encode the form data that is submitted.
Close.formMethod: Indicates the HTTP method used to submit the form.
Close.formNoValidate: Indicates that the form is not to be validated when it is submitted.
Close.formTarget: Overrides the target attribute of the button's form owner.
Close.icon: An icon in place of HeroUI's close mark: an icon name or any icon element.
Close.iconProps: Props for customizing the close icon
Close.isAnimatedStyleActive:
Whether the root's built-in animated styles (react-native-reanimated) are active.
When `false`, the animated scale style is not applied and you can implement custom logic.
Close.isDisabled: True to refuse presses and show the disabled style.
Close.isIconOnly: Whether the button displays an icon only (needed for correct layout)
Close.isPending:
Whether the button is in a pending state. This disables press and hover events
while retaining focusability, and announces the pending state to screen readers.
Close.label: The accessible name in the app's language, for example "Close" or "Dismiss notification".
Close.name: Submitted as a pair with the button's value as part of the form data.
Close.onBlur: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.
Close.onClick:
**Not recommended – use `onPress` instead.** `onClick` is an alias for `onPress`
provided for compatibility with other libraries. `onPress` provides
additional event details for non-mouse interactions.
Close.onFocus: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.
Close.onFocusChange: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.
Close.onHoverChange: Handler that is called when the hover state changes.
Close.onHoverEnd: Handler that is called when a hover interaction ends.
Close.onHoverStart: Handler that is called when a hover interaction starts.
Close.onKeyDown: Handler that is called when a key is pressed.
Close.onKeyUp: Handler that is called when a key is released.
Close.onPress: Called when the button is pressed, by pointer, touch or keyboard.
Close.onPressChange: Handler that is called when the press state changes.
Close.onPressEnd:
Handler that is called when a press interaction ends, either
over the target or when the pointer leaves the target.
Close.onPressStart: Handler that is called when a press interaction starts.
Close.onPressUp:
Handler that is called when a press is released over the target, regardless of
whether it started on the target or not.
Close.preventFocusOnPress:
Whether to prevent focus from moving to the button when pressing it.

Caution, this can make the button inaccessible and should only be used when alternative
keyboard interaction is provided, such as ComboBox's MenuTrigger or a NumberField's
increment/decrement control.
Close.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Close.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop

Close.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
Close.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.
Close.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Close.type: The behavior of the button when used in an HTML form.
Close.value: The value associated with the button's name when it's submitted with the form data.

Modal.aria-describedby: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
Modal.aria-details:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.
Modal.aria-labelledby: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
Modal.background:
Background layer rendered behind the dialog content.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Dialog.ContentBackground`, whose
  content is decided by the active library theme
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely (wrap content in
  `Dialog.ContentBackground` to keep the absolute-fill and clipping)
- `null`: removes the background layer
Modal.children: The modal's parts, usually a header, a body and a footer; any element is allowed.
Modal.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
Modal.forceMount:
Whether to force mount the component in the DOM
Useful for animation purposes when component needs to be present but hidden
Modal.isDismissable:
True, the default, to close the overlay on a press outside it (the backdrop on a modal, a drawer and a dialog).
Set false for a step the user must finish, and give the content its own close control.
Modal.isEntering:
Whether the dialog is currently performing an entry animation. Focus is not moved into the
dialog until the animation completes, since moving the screen reader cursor may cause scrolling
that interrupts the animation.
Modal.isKeyboardDismissDisabled:
True to keep the Escape key from closing the overlay. It is for a flow with unsaved work or a nested overlay
open, so set it only with `isDismissable` false or a close control in reach. Native has no Escape key, so it
stays unread there unless a component's own page says it maps to the Android back button.
Modal.isOpen: The open state, for a controlled overlay; pair it with `onOpenChange`.
Modal.label: The accessible name for a modal that has no `Modal.Title`; with a title, the title names it.
Modal.motion:
How the dialog enters: `slide-up`, `stick-top` (flush with the top) or `slide-side` (from the inline-end side, full
height). Left out, it keeps the runtime's own entrance. A reduced motion level fades it instead.
Modal.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
Modal.position:
The dialog's vertical place on the screen. `auto`, the default, is the runtime's choice (centred, or at the bottom
on a narrow web screen). It is `position` and not `placement`, which ADR 0312 keeps for `Placement`.
Modal.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.
Modal.role: The accessibility role for the dialog.
Modal.size:
The dialog's width: `sm`, `md` or `lg` cap it, and `full` fills the screen for a full-screen presentation.
Defaults to `md`.
Modal.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.

behavior depending on where it is portalled to.

Popover.asChild: Whether to render as a child element
Popover.avoidCollisions: Whether to automatically adjust position to avoid screen edges
Popover.background:
Background layer rendered behind the popover content.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Popover.ContentBackground`, whose
  content is decided by the active library theme
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely (wrap content in
  `Popover.ContentBackground` to keep the absolute-fill and clipping)
- `null`: removes the background layer
Popover.boundaryElement: Element that that serves as the positioning boundary.
Popover.children:
The popover's content: text, a form, a list of actions. Anything the user must be able to dismiss needs a
control of its own when `isDismissable` is false. Plain text is wrapped for the runtime.
Popover.className:
The CSS [className](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/className) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the class based on component state.
Popover.containerPadding:
The placement padding that should be applied between the element and its
surrounding container.
Popover.crossOffset:
The additional offset applied along the cross axis between the element and its
anchor element.
Popover.defaultOpen: The starting open state, for an uncontrolled overlay. Native's own name for it is `isDefaultOpen`.
Popover.disablePositioningStyle:
Whether to disable the automatic positioning styles
Useful when you want to handle positioning manually
Popover.forceMount: Whether to force mount the component in the DOM
Popover.getTargetRect:
Overrides the target element's bounding rectangle. Useful for positioning relative to
a specific point such as the mouse cursor (e.g. context menus) or text selection.
Popover.hasArrow: True to draw an arrow from the content to its trigger. Defaults to false.
Popover.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
Popover.insets: Screen edge insets to respect when positioning
Popover.isDismissable:
True, the default, to close the overlay on a press outside it (the backdrop on a modal, a drawer and a dialog).
Set false for a step the user must finish, and give the content its own close control.
Popover.isEntering: Whether the popover is currently performing an entry animation.
Popover.isExiting: Whether the popover is currently performing an exit animation.
Popover.isKeyboardDismissDisabled:
True to keep the Escape key from closing the overlay. It is for a flow with unsaved work or a nested overlay
open, so set it only with `isDismissable` false or a close control in reach. Native has no Escape key, so it
stays unread there unless a component's own page says it maps to the Android back button.

Popover.maxHeight:
The maxHeight specified for the overlay element.
By default, it will take all space up to the current viewport height.
Popover.offset:
The additional offset applied along the main axis between the element and its
anchor element.
Popover.onBlurWithin: Handler that is called when the target element and all descendants lose focus.
Popover.onFocusWithin: Handler that is called when the target element or a descendant receives focus.
Popover.onFocusWithinChange: Handler that is called when the the focus within state changes.
Popover.onOpenChange: Called with the new state each time the overlay opens or closes, from its trigger, a dismissal or the app.
Popover.placement: The side of the trigger it opens on, by reading direction. The runtime flips it when there is no room.
Popover.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Popover.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.
Popover.scrollRef: A ref for the scrollable region within the overlay.
Popover.shouldFlip:
Whether the element should flip its orientation (e.g. top to bottom or left to right) when
there is insufficient room for it to render completely.
Popover.shouldSkipAnimation:
Whether the popover should appear and disappear without an entry or exit animation. This is
used by components such as PreviewTrigger to skip animations when quickly swapping between
overlays.
Popover.shouldUpdatePosition: Whether the overlay should update its position automatically.
Popover.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
Popover.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.
Popover.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Popover.title:
The popover's heading, which also names it for assistive technology. Without it, name the content with

Popover.trigger:
The pressable that opens the popover, usually a Button. It keeps its own accessible name; the popover only adds
the pressed and expanded state.
Popover.triggerRef:
The ref for the element which the popover positions itself with respect to.

When used within a trigger component such as DialogTrigger, MenuTrigger, Select, etc.,
this is set automatically. It is only required when used standalone.

Content width sizing strategy
- 'content-fit': Auto-size to content width (default)
- 'trigger': Match trigger width exactly
- 'full': 100% width
- number: Fixed width in pixels

PressFeedback.animation:
Animation configuration for the root component.

- Leave `undefined` or `true` for the default built-in scale animation.
- Provide an object with `scale` to customize the built-in scale:

- `undefined`: Use default animations

Switch.onPressStart: Handler that is called when a press interaction starts.
Switch.onPressUp:
Handler that is called when a press is released over the target, regardless of

Table.fixedColumns: Web: the ids of columns that never move: they draw no drag grip and take no drop (a DataTable's tool columns).
Table.hasMore: True while a cursor page after the last row exists; with `onLoadMore` it loads it when the end comes into view.
Table.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
Table.isColumnResizable:
Web: true to give each header a resize handle (pointer, and the keyboard through the column menu's "Resize"); the
columns then take their `width`, `minWidth` and `maxWidth`, and the table scrolls sideways past its width.
Table.isLoading: True while items load: the collection is busy, and shows its loading state in place of the empty one.
Table.isStickyHeader: True to keep the header in view while the rows scroll; the table then scrolls inside `maxHeight`.
Table.isVirtualized:
Web: true to draw only the rows in view (React Aria's Virtualizer), for thousands of rows. The header stays
stuck, the start pins stay stuck, rows take the density's height (measured when `renderRowSpan` is given) and
the scroll area is `maxHeight` tall. A column pinned to the end scrolls with the rest.
Table.items: The items, in order. The collection never sorts or filters them: the query that fetched them did.
Table.label: The spoken name of the table, for example "Orders"; a table without one is anonymous to assistive technology.
Table.loadingLabel: The spoken name of what loads, for example "Loading orders"; it is read only while `isLoading` is true.
Table.maxHeight: The height the rows scroll inside when the header is sticky, as a CSS length. Defaults to `24rem`.
Table.onColumnMove: Web: given, headers can be dragged to reorder the columns; called with the column and its new index.
Table.onColumnResize: Web: called with a column's new width, in CSS pixels, when a resize ends.
Table.onLoadMore: Called when the end of the rows is reached while `hasMore` is true and nothing is loading.
Table.onReorder:
Web: given, each row gets a drag handle in a leading column (pointer, or the keyboard and a screen reader through
React Aria's drag and drop) and a drop calls this with every row in the new order. Controlled: nothing moves
until the app passes the rows back.
Table.onRowAction: Web: called with a row's id when the row is actioned: a press with no selection mode, or Enter on the row.
Table.onSelectionChange: Called with the ids now selected each time the selection changes, in the order the items are in.
Table.onSortChange: Called with the sort a press on a sortable header asks for; the app fetches the rows in that order.
Table.renderCell:
The content of one cell. Left out, a cell shows the text of the row's property named by the column's `id`; give it
to draw a badge, a date or a link, and give the app's own text for each value, as the table adds none.
Table.renderColumnMenu:
Web: what sits at the end of a header, usually the column's menu. `startResize` starts a keyboard resize of the
column (arrows, then Enter or Escape) when the table is resizable.
Table.renderHeader: Web: a header's content in place of its label, when this returns a node (the label stays its name).
Table.renderRowSpan: Web: a row drawn as one cell across every column (an expanded row's detail) when this returns a node.
Table.rowClassName: Web: extra classes of one row, for example a sticky total row.
Table.selectedKeys: The ids of the selected items, for a controlled collection; pair it with `onSelectionChange`.
Table.selectionMode: What a press or Space does: nothing, select one item, or toggle several. Defaults to `none`.
Table.sort:
Every sort key, most significant first, for a multi-sort: the first marks its header as `sortDescriptor` does and
the others show their rank. Given, it wins over `sortDescriptor`.
Table.sortDescriptor: The sort in force, for a controlled table: the rows arrive sorted, and this only marks the header.
Table.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.
Table.variant: The look of the table. Defaults to `primary`.

TreeSelect.selectionMode: `single` (the default) closes on a choice; `multiple` ticks rows and stays open.
TreeSelect.value: The current value, for a controlled field; pair it with `onChange`.
TreeSelect.variant: The look of the trigger: `primary` on the page, `secondary` on a tinted surface. Defaults to `primary`.

TreeView.aria-describedby: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
TreeView.aria-details:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.
TreeView.aria-labelledby: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
TreeView.autoFocus: Whether to auto focus the gridlist or an option.
TreeView.className: Classes added to the tree's root.
TreeView.defaultExpandedKeys: The ids expanded at the start, for an uncontrolled tree.
TreeView.defaultSelectedKeys: The ids selected at the start, for an uncontrolled collection.
TreeView.dependencies: Values that should invalidate the item cache when using dynamic collections.
TreeView.disabledBehavior: Whether `disabledKeys` applies to all interactions, or only selection.
TreeView.disallowEmptySelection: Whether the collection allows empty selection.
TreeView.dragAndDropHooks:
The drag and drop hooks returned by `useDragAndDrop` used to enable drag and drop behavior for
the Tree.
TreeView.escapeKeyBehavior:
Whether pressing the escape key should clear selection in the grid list or not.

Most experiences should not modify this option as it eliminates a keyboard user's ability to
easily clear selection. Only use if the escape key is being handled externally or should not
trigger selection clearing contextually.
TreeView.expandedKeys: The ids of the expanded rows, for a controlled tree; pair it with `onExpandedChange`.
TreeView.isSelectionPropagated:
True with `selectionMode="multiple"`: checking a row checks every row under it, a row is checked once all its
rows are, and a row with only some of its rows checked shows a dash. The selection holds every checked id.
TreeView.keyboardNavigationBehavior:
Whether keyboard navigation to focusable elements within grid list items is
via the left/right arrow keys or the tab key.
TreeView.label: The accessible name of the tree, for example "Chart of accounts".
TreeView.onAction: Called with a row's id when it is activated (pressed, or Enter on web).
TreeView.onExpandedChange: Called with the ids now expanded each time a row opens or closes.
TreeView.onLoadChildren:
Loads the children of a row marked `hasChildren` the first time it is expanded. A spinner row shows while the
promise is pending and the tree keeps the rows it resolves to; a rejection closes the row so it can be tried again.
TreeView.onMove:
Called when rows are dragged (or moved from the keyboard) to a new place: before or after a row, or inside it.
Given, rows can be dragged on web; the tree does not move them itself, so update `items` (`moveTreeNodes` does
it). Native has no dragging and ignores it.
TreeView.onSelectionChange: Called with the ids now selected each time the selection changes, in the order the items are in.
TreeView.render:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.
TreeView.renderEmptyState: Provides content to display when there are no items in the list.
TreeView.selectedKeys: The ids of the selected items, for a controlled collection; pair it with `onSelectionChange`.
TreeView.selectionBehavior: How multiple selection should behave in the tree.
TreeView.selectionMode: What a press or Space does: nothing, select one item, or toggle several. Defaults to `none`.
TreeView.shouldSelectOnPressUp: Whether selection should occur on press up instead of press down.
TreeView.slot:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.
TreeView.style:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.
TreeView.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

TreemapChart.height: The plot's height in pixels; 240 by default.
TreemapChart.label: The chart's accessible name, such as "Revenue by category".
TreemapChart.sort: Orders the categories: largest first, smallest first, or by label; the rows' own order by default.
TreemapChart.valueFormat: How values are written; plain numbers in the locale by default.

Truncate.children: The text to clip and expand.
Truncate.defaultExpanded: The starting state, for an uncontrolled expand.
Truncate.lines: How many lines show while closed; defaults to 3.
Truncate.mode: `expand` (the default) adds Show more and Show less; `tooltip` shows the whole text on hover and focus (web; native expands).

Turnstile.name: The name the token is posted under; Cloudflare's own `cf-turnstile-response` when left out.
Turnstile.onError:
Called with Cloudflare's error code when the challenge fails (a refused visitor, a network error); the form then
has no token, so the server refuses the post.
Turnstile.siteKey: The site key; the app's `VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` when left out.

TwoColumnLayout.aside: The side column's blocks, from top to bottom. Required: a layout with no side column is a SingleColumnLayout.
TwoColumnLayout.children: The main column's blocks, from top to bottom.
TwoColumnLayout.collapseBelow: The breakpoint under which the frame collapses; AppShell defaults to `md` and TwoColumnLayout to `lg`.
TwoColumnLayout.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
TwoColumnLayout.ref:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
TwoColumnLayout.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

Back.children: The visible label in the app's language, for example "Back" or the previous view's name.

View.label: The view's accessible name, read when it is shown and focus moves to it.

ViewStack.defaultView: The id of the view shown first, the bottom of the stack.
ViewStack.onViewChange: Called with the view on top after every push and pop.
ViewStack.transition: How a view enters and leaves. Defaults to `push`; the motion level can lower it to a fade or nothing.

VisuallyHidden.children: What a screen reader reads and the screen does not show, usually translated text.
VisuallyHidden.elementType: The element type for the container.
VisuallyHidden.id: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
VisuallyHidden.isFocusable: Whether the element should become visible on focus, for example skip links.
VisuallyHidden.testID: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

VoiceInput.className: Styles the row that holds the button, the level and the status.
VoiceInput.isDisabled: True to show the button but refuse presses.
VoiceInput.isStatusVisible: False to hide the status line beside the button (it is still announced). Defaults to true.
VoiceInput.label: The button's name while idle. Defaults to the catalogue's "Start recording".
VoiceInput.onRecord:
Called with each finished recording. While a returned promise runs the input shows "Processing", for example
while the app transcribes; a rejection shows the error state.
VoiceInput.onStateChange: Called each time the state changes.
VoiceInput.recorder: The recorder. Defaults to the MediaRecorder driver on web and the mock driver on native.

WaffleChart.className: Classes for the figure, such as a width or margin.
WaffleChart.label: The chart's accessible name and the data table's caption, such as "Visitors, last six months".
WaffleChart.nameKey: The key of each row's part name, matched to a series' `key`.
WaffleChart.palette: The colours parts take by position: the `categorical` set by default, since a waffle tells parts apart by colour.
WaffleChart.series: The series drawn, in legend order.
WaffleChart.showLegend: Shows the legend under the plot; on by default when there are two series or more.
WaffleChart.valueFormat: How values are written: `{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }`, `{ notation: "compact" }`.
WaffleChart.valueKey: The key of each row's value.

WaterfallChart.className: Classes for the figure, such as a width or margin.
WaterfallChart.endLabel: The closing total's name; its value is the start plus every step.
WaterfallChart.height: The plot's height in pixels; 240 by default.
WaterfallChart.label: The chart's accessible name, such as "Profit, Q3 to Q4".
WaterfallChart.showTooltip: Shows the values of the pointed or pressed bar; on by default.
WaterfallChart.start: The opening total, such as last quarter's profit.
WaterfallChart.valueFormat: How values are written; plain numbers in the locale by default.

WheelDatePicker.defaultValue: The starting day, for an uncontrolled picker; defaults to today.
WheelDatePicker.label: The spoken name of the picker.
WheelDatePicker.maxYear: The last year on the year wheel; defaults to 10 years after this one.
WheelDatePicker.minYear: The first year on the year wheel; defaults to 100 years before this one.
WheelDatePicker.onChange: Called with each new day. A day past the end of the new month is moved to its last day.
WheelDatePicker.value: The day, for a controlled picker.

WheelPicker.columns: The wheels, from the reading start.
WheelPicker.defaultValue: The starting keys, for an uncontrolled picker; a column without one starts on its first choice.
WheelPicker.label: The spoken name of the whole picker.
WheelPicker.onChange: Called with every column's key each time a wheel settles on a new choice.
WheelPicker.value: The centred key of each column, by column key, for a controlled picker.
WheelPicker.visibleCount: How many rows show at once, odd; defaults to 5.

WheelTimePicker.defaultValue: The starting time, for an uncontrolled picker; defaults to midnight.
WheelTimePicker.hourCycle: 12 or 24 hours; defaults to the locale's.
WheelTimePicker.label: The spoken name of the picker.
WheelTimePicker.minuteStep: The step of the minute wheel, for example 5 or 15; defaults to 1.
WheelTimePicker.value: The time, for a controlled picker.

WidgetFrame.actions: Controls at the header's end: a range picker, a menu, a link to the full report.
WidgetFrame.controls: A row under the header for the body's own controls: a range or period picker, a filter.
WidgetFrame.data: The numbers behind the body: the "View as table" view, the accessible alternative, and the CSV download.
WidgetFrame.description: A muted line under the title, such as the range shown.
WidgetFrame.emptyText: The empty note; "No data for this range yet" by default.
WidgetFrame.errorText: The error note; "This widget could not load" by default.
WidgetFrame.fileName: The downloads' file name without its extension; the title by default.
WidgetFrame.footer: A row under the body: a "View all" link, a last-updated note.
WidgetFrame.isComparing: Whether the previous period is drawn beside this one; with `onCompareChange`, the controls row shows a switch.
WidgetFrame.isRefreshing: True while fresh data loads behind the current body: a quiet spinner in the header.
WidgetFrame.menu: The overflow menu's entries, in this order; no menu when left out. `csv` and `table` read `data`.
WidgetFrame.onCompareChange: Called when the compare switch is turned on or off.
WidgetFrame.onRefresh: Shows a refresh button in the header that runs it; its icon spins while `isRefreshing` (still under reduced motion).
WidgetFrame.onRetry: Shows a retry button in the error state.
WidgetFrame.onSortChange: Called with the order picked in the sort menu.
WidgetFrame.size: The columns it spans in a 12-column dashboard grid (web); `medium` by default. Native fills the width.
WidgetFrame.sort: The order the body's categories are in; with `onSortChange`, the header shows a sort menu.
WidgetFrame.state: What the body shows; `ready` by default.
WidgetFrame.title: The widget's title; it also names the region.
WidgetFrame.updatedAt: When the data was fetched: the header reads "Updated 2 min ago" in the locale and keeps it current.

YearPicker.calendar: The calendar the years are written in; `islamic-umalqura` adds the Hijri year under each. Defaults to `gregory`.
YearPicker.defaultValue: The starting year, for an uncontrolled picker.
YearPicker.label: The spoken name of the grid.
YearPicker.maxYear: The last year; defaults to 10 years after this one.
YearPicker.minYear: The first year; defaults to 10 years before this one.
YearPicker.value: The chosen Gregorian year, for a controlled picker.
